title: Secure Federal LEASEs Act
official_summary:
Secure Federal Leases from Espionage And Suspicious Entanglements Act or the Secure Federal LEASEs Act

(Sec. 3) This bill instructs the General Services Administration (GSA), the Architect of the Capitol, or any federal agency (other than the Department of Defense and the intelligence community) that has independent statutory leasing authority (federal lessee), before entering into a lease agreement or approving a novation agreement with an entity involving a change of ownership under a lease that will be used for high-security leased space, to require the entity to identify the immediate or highest-level owner of the space and disclose whether that owner is a foreign person or entity, including the country associated with the ownership entity.

A federal lessee shall require the entity to (1) provide such identification and disclosure when first submitting a proposal in response to a solicitation for offers issued by the federal lessee; and (2) update such information annually, including the list of the immediate or highest-level owners of that entity or the information required to be provided related to each such owner.

(Sec. 4) The GSA shall develop a government-wide plan for identifying all immediate, highest-level, or beneficial owners of high-security leased spaces before entering into a lease agreement to accommodate a federal tenant.

(Sec. 5) The bill provides a rule for language in a lease agreement (concerning restriction of access to high-security space) between a federal lessee and an entity to accommodate an agency in a building or improvement used for high-security leased space.

summary.headline: A 2020 law requires federal leasing agencies to check and disclose foreign ownership of landlords who lease high-security office space to the government.
summary.what_it_does: Before the government signs or approves a lease for high-security office space, the landlord must name its top-level owner and say whether that owner is a foreign person or entity, including the country. Landlords must provide this when they first bid on a solicitation and update it every year. The General Services Administration must also create a government-wide plan for identifying owners of high-security leased spaces before leasing space to a federal tenant. The law also sets a rule for lease language that restricts access to high-security space.

who_it_affects.group: Companies and property owners that lease high-security office space to federal agencies
who_it_affects.how: They must disclose their highest-level owners, including whether any are foreign, when bidding and each year after.

who_it_affects.group: General Services Administration and other federal leasing agencies
who_it_affects.how: They must collect and review ownership disclosures and develop a government-wide plan for identifying owners of high-security leased spaces.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that occupy high-security leased space
who_it_affects.how: Leases for the space they use must follow the ownership disclosure process and the rule on access-restriction language.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 31, 2020; the specific effective dates for individual provisions are not stated in the summary provided.
